newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: GPB, STC in Chinese battery JV.
newsitem.headline: GPB, STC in Chinese battery JV.

text.p: Battery maker GP Batteries International Ltd (GPB) said on Monday it had formed a joint venture with South Korean industrial company STC Corp (STC) to produce alkaline batteries in China.
The new venture was called Geewin Industrial Pte Ltd (Geewin), GPB said in a statement.
"The joint venture allows both GP Batteries and STC to share their expertise in battery business and mass production technology," GPB chairman and chief executive Andrew Ng said in the statement.
GPB said Geewin would form a separate production joint venture called Huizhou Modern Battery Ltd (HMBL) in Huizhou, China with the Desay Corporation taking a 15 percent stake.
Under the terms of the deal, the GPB statement said HMBL would invest about U.S. $15 million in a 3,000 sq m plant that would employ about 100 people.
The plant would make AA and AAA alkaline batteries with production expected to begin in the third quarter of 1997, the statement said.
GPB, a unit of Hong Kong-based Gold Peak Industries (Holdings) Ltd, said it owned 80 percent of Geewin, while STC held the balance.
GPB has manufacturing plants in Hong Kong, China, Taiwan, Malaysia and Denmark with marketing and support offices around the world.
STC is one of Korea's major industrial groups and is one of the major supliers to original equipment manufacturer (OEM) battery markets worldwide.
